producer: Media Exchange Server (Go) of Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows, cmd/exchange-vectors
notes: Every case was run against the real exchange server: `input` is what a client sent (the members of the record, or of the enroll envelope for a device), `verdict` is what the server did (accepted, refused with `reason`, or closed: a malformed record closes the stream with no answer), `listed` is the record exactly as an enrolled device of the account reads it from `list`.

The server owns deviceId (forced to the publisher), presence, updatedAt, startedAt (when the client sent none) and the granted publicPort; every other member, known or not, at any depth, comes back verbatim.

A device record is built from the enroll envelope: unknown members of the envelope are not part of the record, a `receiver` block is kept verbatim (an unknown member inside it included), unknown roles are dropped (the roles of 6.1 are the four of the first edition and `clipboard`, item BV), `"receiver":null` is absent.

`drive` is the section 8.1 wrapper around the listed record, and the file name it is written to. A resource carries `access` on Drive only by the user's opt-in (item X of section 15), so the wrapper here is the default: without it. writtenAt is the generation instant; ttlSeconds is the working default of the vectors (1800 for a device or a resource, 120 for a broadcast).

A record is at most 16384 bytes of JSON as delivered (item BS): the members the producer sent plus the ones the server adds - deviceId, presence, updatedAt, startedAt where the producer sent none, the granted publicPort - in the widest form the record is listed in; a device that goes offline has its records listed again with presence `offline`, a byte longer than `online`, and without the live members `access`, `shareId` and `publicPort`. Admission bounds that result before it stores anything, and a record whose delivered form would exceed it is refused with `capacity` and stores nothing.

So `resource-16KiB-exact` (exactly 16384 bytes as sent) is refused; `resource-delivered-16KiB-exact` is the largest plain record that is accepted (listed at 16383 bytes while its device is online, exactly 16384 once it is offline) and `resource-delivered-16KiB-plus-1` one byte more is refused; `resource-16KiB-plus-1` and `broadcast-16KiB-plus-1` are over the bound as sent. A broadcast is bounded the same way with deviceId, updatedAt and startedAt added.

cases.name: device-minimal
cases.note: only the required members: the optional ones are simply absent from the listed record

cases.name: device-full
cases.note: every optional member; receiver.plays and an unknown nested member travel verbatim

cases.name: device-unknown-role
cases.note: a role the server does not know is not kept: only the roles of 6.1 are - the four of the first edition and `clipboard` (item BV), which is kept

cases.name: device-unknown-product
cases.note: an unknown product value is kept and shown raw

cases.name: device-receiver-null
cases.note: a receiver member that is null says nothing: it is absent, not malformed

cases.name: device-receiver-too-many-modes
cases.note: a receiver list of nine entries is above the bound of eight: the enroll is malformed and the stream is closed with no answer

cases.name: resource-minimal
cases.note: the required members; the server fills deviceId, presence and updatedAt

cases.name: resource-full
cases.note: access, shareId and a third-party port request; the granted port replaces the request; presence and deviceId are the server's

cases.name: resource-unknown-members-deep
cases.note: members the server does not know, three levels deep, come back verbatim

cases.name: resource-unknown-kind
cases.note: an unknown kind is stored and listed; a reader shows it as unsupported

cases.name: resource-16KiB-exact
cases.note: a record of exactly 16384 bytes as sent is refused with capacity and stores nothing: the bound is the record as delivered (item BS), and the members the server adds (deviceId, presence, updatedAt) make this one longer than 16384 when it is listed

cases.name: resource-delivered-16KiB-exact
cases.note: the largest record that is accepted: 16292 bytes as sent, listed at 16383 bytes while its device is online and at exactly 16384 once the device is offline (presence `offline` is a byte longer than `online`)

cases.name: resource-delivered-16KiB-plus-1
cases.note: one byte more than the largest accepted record (16293 bytes as sent) is refused with capacity and stores nothing: its delivered form would be 16385 bytes

cases.name: resource-16KiB-plus-1
cases.note: a record one byte over 16 KiB is refused with capacity and stores nothing

cases.name: resource-held-by-another-device
cases.note: the same resourceId from another device of the account is an id-collision

cases.name: resource-published-again-by-its-device
cases.note: the same device publishing a resourceId it holds replaces the record

cases.name: resource-share-id-held-by-another
cases.note: a shareId held by another resource is an id-collision

cases.name: resource-not-an-id
cases.note: a resourceId that is not 16 random bytes in base64url is malformed: the stream is closed

cases.name: broadcast-minimal
cases.note: the required members; the server stamps deviceId, startedAt and updatedAt

cases.name: broadcast-full
cases.note: title, a startedAt of the client's own and a descriptor with the three kinds of endpoint, verbatim

cases.name: broadcast-unknown-members-deep
cases.note: unknown members of the record and of its descriptor travel verbatim

cases.name: broadcast-without-descriptor
cases.note: a broadcast with no descriptor is malformed: the stream is closed with no answer

cases.name: broadcast-16KiB-plus-1
cases.note: a record one byte over 16 KiB is refused with capacity

cases.name: broadcast-held
cases.note: kept live for the two cases below

cases.name: broadcast-id-held-by-another-device
cases.note: the same broadcastId from another device is an id-collision

cases.name: broadcast-started-again-by-its-device
cases.note: the same device starting a broadcastId it holds replaces the record
